TOPIC - COLOURS
LEARNING AREA
Lesson One - Various Colour Around Us and Components of Light - Colour in the Rainbow
Lesson Two - Primary and Secondary Colours
Lesson Three - Revision and Test
TIME - 40 Minutes each.
LEARNING OUTCOME
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. separate white light into the component colours;
2. identify and name the colours of light (rainbow);
name objects that have characteristics of natural colours;
3. collect and list materials that produce colours;
4. sort primary and secondary colours from a collection of coloured plates;
5. identify characteristics of colour shades;
6. mix primary and secondary colours and identify the shades of colours produced.
RATIONALE
Color plays a vitally important role in the world in which we live. In our environment, there are objects of different colours.
The blue, green, red, etc. all these colours are used for different purposes. For example, traffic controls, zebra crossing, beautifying objects, identity or differentiate items (groups), design, marking, etc.
There are two kind of colours - primary and secondary colours.
The concept of colours will enable the pupils to understand and identify different colours and appreciate the importance of colours in our everyday life.
LEARNING MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
Glass prism
White screen or wall
A colour chart
Coloured plates or discs
Flowers
Leaves
Clay soil
Water
Mortar and pestle
Cardboard papers
Crayons
Water colour
Colour filter
Various coloured objects
Colour poster
Colour discs.
PREVIOUS KNOWLEDGE
We all have the colour we like best. One person may like green colour best, another may like blue best and yet another may like red colour best. Every colour has somebody who likes it.
